# E078 -- HCMA Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Brand**: HCMA
- **Industry**: Architecture
- **Year**: 2022
- **Source file**: `4b23e5042384a1fc1b55121c65f3064a.pdf`
- **Pages reviewed**: 1-2, 6-7, 12-13
- **Document version**: Version 01

## Brand Strategy
- **Belief**: Human connections are the best path to solving fundamental problems in the world.
- **Vision**: A future where people and institutions come together to create lasting change.
- **Purpose**: Create shared experiences that ignite conversations and build compassionate communities.
- **Core messaging**: "hcma designs buildings, brands, and shared experiences that connect people. Because with collective strength, communities can work together to make a difference to the issues that matter."
- Strong emphasis on collective strength, inclusive design, biodiversity, and minimizing environmental impact.

## Logo
- Detailed logo section covering: anatomy, aspect ratio, minimum size, clear space, co-branding, and no-goes.
- Company name must always be written in lowercase ("hcma", never "HCMA").
- Avatar system also documented with anatomy, usage, aspect ratio, minimum size, clear space, frame space, and no-goes.
- Lockup variants: solo-branding, co-branding, internal initiatives.
- Tagline treated as a display element with its own rules.

## Typography
- Three typeface tiers: primary, secondary, and graphic typeface.
- Hand annotations also addressed as a typographic element.
- Numerals and symbols have their own section.
- Type style guide with rules and typesetting addresses.
- Sentence case enforced for headings (no Title Case).

## Color
- Primary palette plus extended palette.
- Colour pairings and sub-palettes defined.
- Specific rules for logo-on-colour and avatar-on-colour usage.
- Colour-in-use examples provided.

## Graphics
- Graphic forms, patterns, graphic style, and artworks.
- Logo used as a graphic element.
- "Squircle" as a distinct brand shape.
- Organization graphics documented.

## Photography
- Imagery overview with multiple categories: primary portraits, candid portraits, group portraits, city life.
- "Artefacts" split into process and product photography.
- Photography no-goes provided.

## Applications
- Letterhead, business cards, compliment cards, notebooks/sketch books, forms.

## Tone of Voice
- Voice adjusts by audience (industry experts vs. general) and context (social media = informal, proposals/award entries = formal).
- Active voice preferred; contractions encouraged for warmth.
- Avoid empty adjectives ("beautiful", "amazing") -- focus on people/community benefit.
- Sentence case for headings; bullet points to break up text.
- Exclamation marks used sparingly (one per piece).
- "eg"/"ie" without periods, or prefer "for example".

## Outliers
- Indigenous languages addressed as a dedicated section in the verbal identity -- unusual and progressive for an architecture firm.
- "Squircle" as a named brand shape element is distinctive.
- The company name is always lowercase even in running text, enforced typographically.
- Extensive avatar system beyond a simple logo -- uncommon depth.

## Quality Score
4/5 -- Comprehensive document covering verbal identity, visual identity, and applications with notable depth in voice guidelines and photography direction. The TOC indicates ~95 pages of content, well-structured with clear section hierarchy.
